proposed_comments.title: Guard queued selection publication by the current selection generation
proposed_comments.body:
### Guard queued selection publication by the current selection generation

**Severity:** `high`

The asynchronous selection path can still publish details or a suggestion after a newer selection has won: the cancellation token is checked before the background work and before the first publication, but the queued UI callbacks do not carry a selection generation, and the details object is read before the UI callback runs. Increment a generation whenever the selected item changes or is cleared, capture it for this request, and re-check it inside every UI callback; read `item.Details` inside the callback before sending `ShowDetailsMessage`. Keep the hide-details and suggestion notifications on the same guarded UI path so an older selection cannot overwrite the current result.

confidence.rationale: The pinned upstream method checks only the cancellation token around background work, while the converged fork adds a selection generation and moves details and suggestion publication behind guarded UI callbacks.

proposed_comments.title: Publish queued selection failure after marking the item unhealthy
proposed_comments.body:
### Publish queued selection failure after marking the item unhealthy

**Severity:** `medium`

If selected-property initialization throws, the current catch closes the lifetime but leaves the item without the error flag and completes the waiting task in `finally`. That lets a queued caller observe completion before the failure state and before notifications raised by initialization have drained. Mark the item as errored, complete the task with `false` on the failure path, and queue successful completion through the lifetime after initialization notifications have finished; expose the protected error-state transition from `CommandItemViewModel`.

confidence.rationale: The upstream catch/finally sequence is directly visible at the pinned RIGHT-side range, and the converged fix changes both the error state and completion ordering.

proposed_comments.title: Refresh non-observable details through a replacement graph
proposed_comments.body:
### Refresh non-observable details through a replacement graph

**Severity:** `high`

For a matching non-observable details model, reinitializing the existing `DetailsViewModel` mutates the live graph in place. If a later property or child read fails, the healthy graph can be partially torn down and its existing subscribers lose their content. Build a replacement `DetailsViewModel`, initialize it before publishing, clean it up and report the exception if initialization fails, then swap it in and clean up the previous graph only after the replacement succeeds; keep the current in-place refresh behavior for observable details.

confidence.rationale: The pinned upstream branch reuses the existing graph for the matching-model path, while the converged fork adds a replacement-and-rollback path and a focused failure test.

proposed_comments.title: Clean up tags that initialized before a later tag failed
proposed_comments.body:
### Clean up tags that initialized before a later tag failed

**Severity:** `medium`

The current LINQ projection initializes each `TagViewModel` but does not clean up the earlier view models if a later tag throws. Build the list in a temporary collection, clean every already-created view model in a catch block, and assign `Tags` only after the complete collection has initialized so a failed refresh cannot leak subscriptions or expose a partial list.

confidence.rationale: The failure window is localized to the changed projection, and the converged fork replaces it with explicit two-phase construction and cleanup.

proposed_comments.title: Serialize foreground-rights calls with extension disposal
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: ExtensionWrapper.cs is fork-only and has no current RIGHT-side anchor in PR 50398.
proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize foreground-rights calls with extension disposal

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:**
`src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Models/ExtensionWrapper.cs`, `ExtensionWrapper.TryAllowSetForeground(bool)` and the `SignalDispose`, `GetExtensionObject`, and `IsRunning` lifetime paths.

**Problem:**
The current method reads `_extensionObject` and checks liveness outside the wrapper lock, then uses the native WinRT pointer while another thread may dispose and clear the object. That creates a disposal/use race and can pass a stale native pointer to `CoAllowSetForegroundWindow`.

**Why it matters:**
Foreground activation can fail intermittently during extension shutdown or concurrent provider calls, and the existing exception handler cannot make a use-after-dispose window safe.

**Suggested change:**
1. Enter `_lock` before checking liveness or reading `_extensionObject`.
2. Return `false` when the selected object is null; otherwise keep the lock while converting it to `IWinRTObject`, calling `CoAllowSetForegroundWindow`, retaining it with `GC.KeepAlive`, and logging a failing HRESULT.
3. Preserve the existing outer exception log and do not expose the object or release the lock between selecting it and the native call.

**Verification:**
Add or run a focused concurrency test that races `TryAllowSetForeground(true)` with `SignalDispose()` and verifies no stale object is used, then build the CmdPal ViewModels project.

confidence.rationale: The fork-only implementation adds exactly this lock scope, and the wrapper's disposal and native-call paths share the same `_lock` as the current object state.

proposed_comments.title: Keep regression coverage for the queued lifecycle failures
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The fork-only test additions are not a safe standalone production-code suggestion and several test helpers are outside the current RIGHT-side ranges.
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep regression coverage for the queued lifecycle failures

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:**
`src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/DetailsLifecycleTests.cs`, especially the queued-selection, non-observable refresh, and tracked-model helper tests.

**Problem:**
The current upstream test file does not cover the newly identified failure windows: a queued selection that throws, a property notification that must precede selection completion, a failed non-observable snapshot refresh that must preserve the original graph, or cleanup of partially initialized tags.

**Why it matters:**
Without these tests, later lifecycle changes can silently reintroduce stale UI publication, leaked subscriptions, or destructive refresh failures while the main happy-path tests continue to pass.

**Suggested change:**
1. Block initialization, queue selection, force a details failure, and assert `SafeSlowInitAsync()` is false and `IsInErrorState` is true.
2. Block a queued property notification and assert the selection task remains incomplete until the notification is released.
3. Make a snapshot details body read throw and assert the original `DetailsViewModel` and content remain subscribed while the error is reported.
4. Make a later tag initialization throw and assert every previously created tag is cleaned up; keep helper failure hooks deterministic and release all gates in `finally` blocks.

**Verification:**
Run `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests` and confirm the focused lifecycle tests pass without leaked subscribers or hung tasks.

confidence.rationale: The converged fork adds these exact regression scenarios and the stated assertions directly exercise the production failure paths.
